title: Cortland Associates Inc. MO Has $719,000 Position in Apple (AAPL)
text:
Tweet 
Cortland Associates Inc. MO boosted its holdings in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 28.6% during the 4th quarter, HoldingsChannel.com reports. The institutional investor owned 4,250 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after acquiring an additional 945 shares during the quarter. Apple accounts for approximately 0.1% of Cortland Associates Inc. MO’s portfolio, making the stock its 24th largest position. Cortland Associates Inc. MO’s holdings in Apple were worth $719,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period. 
A number of other hedge funds and other institutional investors have also made changes to their positions in the stock. Capital Research Global Investors increased its stake in Apple by 15.0% in the second quarter. Capital Research Global Investors now owns 29,449,961 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $4,241,383,000 after purchasing an additional 3,845,363 shares in the last quarter. Legal & General Group Plc increased its stake in Apple by 1.1% in the third quarter. Legal & General Group Plc now owns 26,393,202 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $4,067,559,000 after purchasing an additional 287,027 shares in the last quarter. Janus Henderson Group PLC increased its stake in Apple by 9.3% in the third quarter. Janus Henderson Group PLC now owns 21,854,159 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $3,367,571,000 after purchasing an additional 1,850,572 shares in the last quarter. Schwab Charles Investment Management Inc. increased its stake in Apple by 3.1% in the fourth quarter. Schwab Charles Investment Management Inc. now owns 19,262,302 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $3,259,868,000 after purchasing an additional 570,279 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Swiss National Bank increased its stake in Apple by 0.4% in the third quarter. Swiss National Bank now owns 19,248,516 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $2,966,581,000 after purchasing an additional 79,100 shares in the last quarter. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 61.35% of the company’s stock. 
NASDAQ:AAPL opened at $165.72 on Monday. Apple has a 52 week low of $141.85 and a 52 week high of $183.50. The stock has a market cap of $840,865.50, a P/E ratio of 17.99, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.26 and a beta of 1.25. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a current ratio of 1.24. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 EPS for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The business had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. During the same period last year, the firm earned $3.36 earnings per share. Apple’s revenue for the quarter was up 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. equities research analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.3 earnings per share for the current year. 
In related news, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction dated Friday, April 13th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total transaction of $6,833,048.52. Following the transaction, the insider now directly owns 64,475 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $11,261,203.50. The transaction was disclosed in a legal filing with the SEC, which is available through this hyperlink . Also, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, April 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total transaction of $2,938,460.00. Following the transaction, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares in the company, valued at $11,194,221.92. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last ninety days, insiders have sold 125,988 shares of company stock worth $21,336,201. 0.08% of the stock is owned by insiders. 
AAPL has been the subject of several research reports. Rosenblatt Securities set a $180.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Tuesday, December 26th. Wells Fargo reissued a “hold” rating and set a $195.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday, December 27th. ValuEngine raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a research report on Sunday, December 31st. Piper Jaffray reissued a “buy” rating and set a $200.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Tuesday, January 2nd. Finally, Zacks Investment Research raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $190.00 price objective for the company in a research report on Wednesday, January 3rd. Two equities research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty-two have issued a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the stock. The stock currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $203.15.
